**Publish gate report: search ad**

**Going out:** Google-style search ad for Pebblebrook Tea Co., UK, headline and description as drafted.

**Claims check**
| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| "Monthly loose leaf tea" | Product fact, fine |
| "If your box isn't right, we'll make it right." | **Unproven.** This is an implied satisfaction guarantee/remedy. The policy bans guarantees and says we have no such offer. Not on the allowlist. |
| "Free UK delivery on orders over £25" | On the policy list (shipping policy) |

**Regulated claims:** No health, money, environment or children issues. The "make it right" line promises a remedy (refund or replacement), which is the kind of promise that needs a real policy behind it.

**House style:** No banned words or AI tells. Tone is plain and warm. The headline "Tea Subscription UK" is keyword-style but acceptable for search. Score about 90.

**Disclosure:** Paid search ad from our own account is marked by the platform, so no extra label needed.

**Fixed:** Nothing applied yet. I haven't swapped in new wording because the right replacement depends on what you actually offer.

**Needs a decision**
- Remove "If your box isn't right, we'll make it right." My suggestion is to replace it with a claim from the policy: "Subscribers can pause or cancel any time." Suggested version:
  Headline: Tea Subscription UK | Description: Monthly loose leaf tea. Pause or cancel any time. Free UK delivery on orders over £25.
- If there is a real returns or remedy policy, add it to the brand policy with its terms and then it can be used.

**Approver:** Sam (marketing lead). Approval needs to be an explicit yes to the exact final wording. Nothing is approved yet, so this should not go out as drafted.
